A: Panel A is CD3 immunofluorescence of RE hemispherectomy cortex showing perivascular T-cell cuffing around vessel, directly supporting perivascular cytotoxic inflammation in Rasmussen encephalitis. C: Panel C is merged CD3/TCR γδ image confirming perivascular cytotoxic T-cell inflammation in RE brain parenchyma. D: Panel D is CD3 immunofluorescence showing large cluster of T cells within RE cortical parenchyma, representing cytotoxic T-cell inflammation. E: Panel E is TCR γδ immunofluorescence of same parenchymal cluster, showing γδ subset of cytotoxic infiltrate. F: Panel F is merged image confirming parenchymal cytotoxic T-cell cluster with γδ T cells in RE cortex.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is axial non-contrast CT showing right hemispheric hypodense area with sulcal widening and ex-vacuo ventricular dilatation, captioned as Rasmussen encephalitis volume loss. B: Panel B is axial non-contrast CT showing same right hemispheric hypodensity and volume loss attributed to Rasmussen encephalitis in caption. C: Panel C is axial post-contrast CT confirming absence of pathological enhancement within right hemispheric hypodense lesions, consistent with non-enhancing pattern in Rasmussen encephalitis, with persistent atrophy/dilatation visible. D: Panel D is axial post-contrast CT confirming absence of enhancement in right hemispheric lesion, consistent with Rasmussen encephalitis, with visible hemispheric volume loss.

panels.figure_caption: Brain CT scan Axial non-contrast CT images (A, B) demonstrate a right hemispheric cortico-subcortical hypodense area (★), not confined to any vascular territory, associated with widening of the right cortical sulci and ex-vacuo dilatation of the right lateral ventricle, reflecting parenchymal volume loss in the adjacent cerebral hemisphere. Axial post-contrast CT images (C, D) confirm the absence of pathological enhancement within the right hemispheric hypodense lesions (★), consistent with the non-enhancing pattern characteristically observed in Rasmussen encephalitis.

panels.figure_caption: Follow-up brain MRI findings during the second admission (A, B, C) Axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images demonstrate extensive left hemispheric cortico-subcortical hyperintensities (★), not confined to any vascular territory, with diffuse cortical thickening and ipsilateral pulvinar involvement (arrows in B). (D) Coronal T2-weighted image shows diffuse left hemispheric cortical thickening (★) and contralateral right sulcal widening with passive dilatation of the right lateral ventricle (arrows), reflecting chronic right hemispheric volume loss without signal abnormality. (E, F) Axial diffusion-weighted images (DWI) demonstrate diffusion restriction within the left hemispheric cortico-subcortical lesions (★), reflecting excitotoxic cellular swelling and early inflammatory necrosis. (G) Axial apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) map confirms true diffusion restriction within the left hemispheric lesions (★), with corresponding signal reduction. (H) Coronal T1-weighted post-contrast image shows the absence of pathological enhancement within the left hemispheric signal abnormalities.
in_text_mentions: n MRI demonstrated the new onset of a diffuse T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity encompassing the left cerebral hemisphere, associated with prominent cortical thickening and significant diffusion restriction, without any abnormal contrast enhancement following intravenous gadolinium administration. This acute involvement extended to the left thalamus and hippocampus, while the posterior fossa structures were completely spared. Concurrently, it confirmed marked right cerebral atrophy with widening of the ipsilateral sulci, representing the chronic sequelae of the initial hemispheric insult (Figure 3).

There is a tendency of association between disease duration and atrophy severity, as shown in Figure 1 and Figure 2. It is worth noting that atrophy also progressed after surgery in patients 3 (Figure 5) and 8 (Figure 6), despite their positive seizure and EPC outcome.
